pillars.name: Strategy and leadership
pillars.nextStep: Agree two or three business problems AI should help with, name an owner for each and decide how you will measure success.

pillars.name: Data
pillars.nextStep: Move your most important records, such as customers, sales and stock, into one shared digital place, and agree who keeps them up to date.

pillars.name: Technology
pillars.nextStep: Fix the basics first: reliable devices and connectivity for key staff, and a simple way for your main tools to share information.

pillars.name: People and skills
pillars.nextStep: Give your team short, practical sessions on everyday AI tools, and make time for people to practise on their real work.

pillars.name: Processes
pillars.nextStep: Map one important workflow from start to finish before automating anything, and agree what ‘better’ will look like.

pillars.name: Governance and responsible use
pillars.nextStep: Write a one-page AI use guide: which tools staff may use, which data must never go into them and who approves new tools.

levels.name: Ready to scale
levels.summary: You have strong foundations. The opportunity now is to scale what works, with clear measures and good governance.

levels.name: Ready to pilot
levels.summary: You are ready to test AI on one or two well-chosen problems. A focused pilot will show what works before you invest more.

levels.name: Building foundations
levels.summary: Some foundations are in place. Strengthening the weaker areas first will make any AI investment far more likely to pay off.

levels.name: Getting started
levels.summary: You are at the beginning, which is a good place to make sound choices. Start with the basics below before buying any AI tool.
